subject: Urgent: CrimsonAI retry flood — SLA credits & remediation plan
messages:
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.meyers@crimsonai.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Retry flood / 5xx spike impacting production — urgent help needed

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a large spike of 500/429 responses and timeouts on our production traffic to the Redwood API around 07:40 PDT this morning. Latency climbed from our baseline (~120ms p50) to >800ms, and our client retries created what looks like a retry flood — we're seeing client-side queues back up and 30% error rate on some routes. This is causing degraded functionality for our customers and we're getting executive pressure.

Can you confirm you see the same on your side and advise immediate mitigations? We need:
- Quick mitigation to stop the retry storm (suggested: circuit break or rate throttle)
- Root cause summary and ETA for fix
- A clear compensation proposal or credit given SLA impact (this is blocking our renewal discussion)

I've attached our internal error timeline and a short clip from our dashboard. Happy to jump on a call — Sophie and Jordan are available.

Thanks,
Sophie Lambert
VP of Product, CrimsonAI
Sophie.Lambert@crimsonai.com
(attachment: crimsonai-error-timeline.png)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>, Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@crimsonai.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retry flood / 5xx spike impacting production — urgent help needed

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. We see the same spike in 5xx/429 on the routes you referenced (model: rdw-2-large / inference path v1). Our SREs have flagged a retry amplification pattern starting at ~07:35 PDT that correlates with an upstream caching TTL change and sudden traffic reshaping on your side.

Immediate actions taken (already in motion):
- Enabled short-term request queue shedding and per-customer concurrent request cap for your org to limit amplification
- Rolled back a non-essential kernel optimization that was degrading tail latency in a small subset of hosts
- Opened SUP-9876 (internal) to track the remediation work and log aggregation (link: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9876)

Next steps we propose:
1) A technical post-mortem with SRE+Crimson engineering within 48 hours.
2) A temporary 30% invoice credit for the affected 6-hour window while we finish a deeper root-cause analysis — pending leadership approval.
3) Follow-up: additional monitoring dashboards and a recommended retry/backoff policy that we've prepared for you.

I'll escalate for approval on the credit immediately and loop in Finance/Sales to finalize numbers. Monica — can you pull the token/usage accounting for CRIM-4521 and attach the breakdown? Lauren/Markus — please advise on credit process and external comms cadence.

Rishi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood-internal-alerts-07-25.png)

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>, Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@crimsonai.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retry flood / 5xx spike impacting production — urgent help needed

Folks, attaching the raw usage and error breakdown for CRIM-4521 across the affected window (07:30–13:30 PDT). Key points:
- Total requests: 2,140,312 in window
- Error volume: 489,120 (22.9% overall); 5xxs and 429s concentrated on /generate and /chat endpoints
- Estimated billable tokens impacted: ~18.4M tokens

I've included a short per-route CSV and the aggregated logs in the zip (crimsonai-logs-2026-07-25.zip). The temporary caps Rishi flipped reduced error rate to ~6% within 10 minutes.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood
monica.patel@redwood.ai
(attachments: crimsonai-logs-2026-07-25.zip, per-route-breakdown.csv)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retry flood / 5xx spike impacting production — urgent help needed

Team — for external comms and invoicing: I recommend we offer an initial good-faith credit of 40% for the 6-hour impacted window, then open the books for a precise credit after RCA. Reasoning: Crimson is a strategic account (deal CRIM-4521 in late-stage renewal), and offering a stronger immediate credit reduces churn risk.

If leadership signs off we'll draft a concise external note: what happened, what we did, credit amount, and preventative commitment. Markus — do you want to take point with exec outreach?

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
(attachment: SLA-credits-draft.docx)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retry flood / 5xx spike impacting production — urgent help needed

Rishi/Team — I just briefed VP Ops and we want to fast-track an executive call with Crimson leadership. Please lock a 30–45 minute slot tomorrow morning PDT.

On credits: temporary 40% is acceptable as a starting point, but we should cap the immediate commitment to the one billing cycle and reserve right to adjust once RCA completes. Also recommend a technical remediation credit (3 months of enhanced monitoring) to rebuild trust.

Sean — please prepare a short exec slide (3 slides) summarizing timeline, impact, and proposed credit so we can present on the call.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>, Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@crimsonai.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed remediation & credit: CrimsonAI (CRIM-4521)

Hi Sophie and Jordan — following our internal review and the initial fixes, here is Redwood's proposed path forward: 

1) Immediate: one-time 40% credit applied to the invoice covering 07:30–13:30 PDT on 2026-07-25 (est. token impact 18.4M). This will appear as a billing adjustment once Finance processes the case.
2) Near-term: SRE-led post-mortem with Crimson engineering within 48 hours. We'll share logs, timeline, and mitigation plan.
3) Preventative: complimentary 3-month enhanced monitoring package (no extra cost) and a joint retry/backoff policy doc we will help implement.
4) Follow-up: final credit reconciliation pending RCA and token accounting (we reserve right to reconcile +/- 10% based on final counts).

If these terms are acceptable we will: schedule the exec brief, issue a draft credit memo for your review, and begin the RCA process.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand the impact and are committed to a prompt, transparent resolution.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-internal-alerts-07-25.png)

From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@crimsonai.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@crimsonai.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed remediation & credit: CrimsonAI (CRIM-4521)

Rishi — thank you. The proposal reads fair and shows good faith. We accept the one-time 40% credit and the 3-month monitoring commitment. We'd like the RCA within the 48-hour window you cited and a recording of the exec brief. Once we get the official credit memo we will route to procurement and finance.

Please add Jordan and me to the RCA invite and include any dashboards you plan to share.

Sophie Lambert
VP of Product, CrimsonAI
